A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BoostedProb study. Their full text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison; retained content can be matched across moves and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original QE experiments across translation, summarization and question answering, together with ablations and a human analysis of valid output tokens.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds SciEx evaluation, LLM self-judge comparisons, Qwen-based evaluation and a five-seed NLLB experiment.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same significant-drop heuristic, dominant-cluster probability-mass scoring and stated mean aggregation. The selected thresholds remain x=30% and epsilon=0.005. Added theory and decoding disclosures do not establish a change to the proposed QE procedure.

E1.justification: SciEx adds English/German university-exam question answering alongside the existing English GSM8K mathematics task (Tables 1 and 3). Translation, summarization and ASR coverage remain. Fleurs zh-en becoming cmn-en in Table 3 is a relabeling of the retained Chinese evaluation.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds LLM self-judge comparisons for Bloomz 560M and Llama 3.2 3B on summarization and mathematics QA. Existing Monte Carlo, probability, entropy, supervised and perturbation-based comparators remain. Qwen-based judging in Appendix E supplies evaluation targets rather than another QE comparator.

E3.justification: v3 introduces an NLLB experiment using top-p sampling with p=0.5 and adds Qwen2.5 72B Instruct judging as an evaluation target for summarization and QA. LLM self-judge introduces an additional scoring pass. Newly specified beam and greedy decoding for existing experiments are disclosures, without evidence that their previous protocols changed.

E4.justification: New Appendix D examines sensitivity to stochastic inference on NLLB. Appendix E extends the existing evaluation-metric checks with Qwen-based judgments. The dominant-token, aggregation, hyperparameter, model-strength, hallucination and less-ambiguous-task analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix D newly reports five NLLB sampling runs using seeds 0–4 and plus/minus variability summaries in Table 9. This is an explicitly additional experiment, not evidence that every retained experiment was repeated. The precise statistic represented by the plus/minus values is not clearly defined.

E6.justification: Matched existing result values remain unchanged. Additions include SciEx correlations, self-judge scores, Qwen-based correlations and sampled NLLB summaries. For example, Table 4 reports Llama 3.2 QA self-judge at 0.232 versus BoostedProb at 0.111. Table 3's reported probability/entropy/BoostedProb averages change from 0.092/0.221/0.286 to 0.083/0.208/0.268 over expanded coverage, not comparable-setting performance deterioration.

T1.justification: New Appendix B provides a short idealized derivation: if each of k correct tokens receives at least p_min, normalization implies p_min <= 1/k; their combined mass can instead approach one. This adds formal reasoning beyond v2's qualitative motivation, but does not establish correctness of the estimated dominant clusters.

C1.justification: The abstract, numbered contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about underconfidence, inexpensive probability boosting, advantages over raw probability, competitiveness with costlier QE methods in some settings, and stronger models' self-evaluation. Additional experiments support rather than redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Section 6.1 newly explains applicability across decoding methods and attributes Tower's self-judge failures to its lack of training for that scoring task. Section 5.5.1 more explicitly characterizes automatic evaluation scores as pseudo ground truth. Existing weak-model and low-ambiguity limitations remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds an implementation repository pointer and specifies beam size 4 for Whisper/DeltaLM and greedy decoding for other models. It also identifies the Qwen judging model. These improve documented reproducibility; the PDFs do not establish reruns of retained experiments. Existing software and A100 40GB hardware disclosures remain.

R1.justification: References are added for SciEx, BART, ROUGE, Qwen2.5 and LLM-as-a-Judge, with the latter motivating a new comparison. The related-work discussion and positioning against probability-based, supervised and ensemble QE remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized language corrections and adds explanatory paragraphs, acknowledgements, and theory and randomness appendices. Existing appendices are relabeled accordingly. The main section sequence and most retained prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1 and 3 gain SciEx rows, Table 4 gains a self-judge column, and a new variability table is inserted. The former Table 9 becomes an expanded Table 10. Existing figures retain their content, while table sizing, float placement and page layout change.

improvement.justification: Broader QA evaluation, self-judge and metric checks, the five-seed study, and code/decoding disclosures provide a modest net gain in evidence and reproducibility. Reporting weaknesses limit that gain: the abstract and Section 6.1 retain average-improvement figures inconsistent with expanded Table 3, and Appendix B describes a bound on the common minimum probability too broadly as a cap on each correct token. The core empirical evidence remains intact.
